title: CANCEL — release a called program from memory; next CALL re-initialises its WORKING-STORAGE
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. RESETTABLE-COUNTER.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-OUT  PIC 9(4).
      *> A called program retains its WORKING-STORAGE between calls
      *> by default. CANCEL releases the program from memory; the
      *> NEXT CALL re-initialises everything. Legacy 'reset counter'
      *> idiom: CALL COUNTER; CALL COUNTER; CANCEL COUNTER; CALL
      *> COUNTER -- third call starts at zero.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           CALL "COUNTER".
           CALL "COUNTER".
           CANCEL "COUNTER".
           CALL "COUNTER".
notes: CANCEL is the COBOL way to reset stateful subprograms. A Java rewrite to 'new Subprogram()' inverts the default — the spec must capture which calls intentionally retain state and which reset.
